newsitem.title: FRANCE: Exiled prince vows return to Cambodia, even jail.
newsitem.headline: Exiled prince vows return to Cambodia, even jail.

text.p: Exiled Cambodian Prince Norodom Sirivudh says he cannot afford to live in France and says he intends to return home even if jailed because that would provide him with free meals.
"You see, if I'm going back, it is also for financial reasons because I can no longer afford to live in France," Sirivudh told the French weekly Le Point in an interview published on Friday.

"In prison, at least, you eat free of charge," said Sirivudh, King Norodom Sihanouk's half-brother who was exiled to France nearly a year ago to avoid a 10-year prison sentence for an alleged plot to kill second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
The prince said his return, whose timing he was keeping secret, was driven by political considerations.
"It will be a political return. The Cambodian people are waiting for me," he said.
His proposed return has become a political tangle.
Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh has formally asked Sihanouk to pardon Sirivudh, but the king said he would not grant amnesty to Sirivudh without the approval of Hun Sen.
Hun Sen, who had threatened to call out troops and tanks to prevent Sirivudh's return, later relented and said he would welcome him with flowers if he were given a royal amnesty.
